column1: # THE TREE VIEW (`aontu view tree`, docs/design/VIEWS.0.md): the
# dependency tree of one document's link graph, drawn as text.
# The reference implementation was the `tree` kind of
# use-cases/tools/diagram.js, whose output use-case 16 pins as goldens;
# those goldens are the acceptance test for the port, and these rows
# are the shared contract behind them: the rendered TEXT, byte for byte,
# and the refusals.
# Four columns: name, view, src, expect. The options ride `expect.ask`
# as {relation?, root?} for the reason reaches' endpoints do -- the
# same document draws differently under a relation filter or from a
# named root. The rest of `expect` is the report: {kind, text} on
# `rendered`, {kind, errors} on `error`, each error minus its prose.
# What the rows pin:
#   - a declared inverse pair (dependsOn / usedBy) collapses to ONE edge,
#     drawn under the named relation, or under the code-point-least key
#     with every key in the label when no relation is named;
#   - a shared subtree is expanded once and marked `(*)` after, and only
#     where it has children of its own -- a repeated leaf is just a leaf;
#   - an edge that closes a loop is marked `(cycle)` and not walked;
#   - a root is a node nothing depends on, a self-edge notwithstanding,
#     and a component with no such node is drawn from its least label;
#   - a named root draws its subtree alone, duplicates once, and a root
#     that is not a node of the DRAWN graph is a refusal
#     (refer_unresolved), as is a relation with no edges
#     (view_relation_unknown); a document with no edges draws nothing,
#     which is a rendering and not a refusal;
#   - an empty relation name means every relation, in both ports;
#   - a label is the shortest trailing path suffix unique in the drawing.
# Every expectation below was obtained by running BOTH CLIs
# (AGENTS.md, "The parity probe").
